Hi Jane — thanks for laying this out. Short answers up front, followed by the recommended playbook for your pilot -> committed path.

Quick answers: 
- Yes: you can start on AWS Marketplace (SaaS subscription) for fast procurement and consolidated AWS billing, then transition to a direct Redwood enterprise contract for Dedicated capacity. We provide migration tooling and can map entitlements so the pilot usage is deducted against later commitments to avoid double-billing.
- Marketplace + MSA: we support listing via marketplace for the pilot and a separate MSA for enterprise terms. In practice, invoices for marketplace purchases come from AWS; committed capacity contracts are invoiced by Redwood (or Redwood via reseller if needed). We document this in the MAP and include a clause to credit marketplace spend toward the first committed period.
- Co-sell and timing: co-sell approval (AWS GTM/co-sell) typically takes 2–4 weeks once the AWS AE has submitted the opportunity. For small pilots we usually do not wait for co-sell approval — marketplace gets the pilot running. Co-sell is most valuable for committed deals (Dedicated).

Recommended playbook (pilot -> committed):
1) Pilot (fastest): Purchase a 30-day SaaS subscription via AWS Marketplace on 5/15. Benefits: consolidated billing, procurement signoff usually faster, no immediate Redwood MSA required for a short pilot.
2) Parallel: We open a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and draft the Redwood MSA + SOW for committed Dedicated capacity in parallel with the pilot. This shortens transition time if you choose to commit.
3) Credit flow: We will apply published marketplace spend as a credit toward the first committed invoice per terms in the MAP. We draft this clause into the MSA/SOW.
4) Co-sell: If you want AWS co-sell for the committed purchase, we engage AWS AE (Michael CC'd) early; co-sell approval takes 2–4 weeks but does not block the pilot.
5) Transition: Ongo-live migration plan — we handle entitlement reconciliation and a single cutover window to avoid double-billing.

Next steps: I attached a short checklist and a MAP template. If this sounds good, can I confirm procurement's must-haves (billing entity, required PO process, any PII cross-border clauses) so the legal team can prioritize the MSA draft?

Thanks,
